trust_decision.summary: Before the updatePost resolver writes, the caller must hold the post type's primitive edit_posts capability, must match the existing post author (or hold edit_others_posts), and - as the published fix adds - must also pass the object-level edit_post meta capability for that post id (which WP maps to edit_published_posts for published posts) and must hold publish_posts whenever the requested post_status is anything other than draft or pending. The decision is taken inside the update{PostType} mutateAndGetPayload closure, immediately before wp_update_post().

landing_point.why: An engineer who read only 'Contributor can publish and modify posts without the required capabilities via updatePost' lands on the 'Stop now if a user isn't allowed to edit posts' guard at the top of the updatePost resolver, then walks the neighbouring edit_others_posts guards and the prepare_post_object()/wp_update_post() call at lines 161-173.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Media items are attachments, not posts: they have their own mutation class, their own MediaItemStatusEnum with no publish state, and are excluded from the PostObjectUpdate registration loop (TypeRegistry.php:447), so the draft/publish editorial capability rules 'obviously' do not apply to updateMediaItem.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: createPost with status PUBLISH by a user lacking publish_posts must silently downgrade to 'pending' and return no error; this is asserted by the pinned test suite. A fix that rejects non-draft/pending status centrally (e.g. in PostObjectMutation::prepare_post_object(), shared by create and update) breaks it.

O6_input_shapes: status omitted entirely (fix uses isset(), so no publish check fires and only the edit_post gate applies)
status = draft or pending (explicitly allowed without publish_posts)
status = PUBLISH, PRIVATE, FUTURE or any custom registered status (rejected without publish_posts)
status = TRASH (also rejected, since it is not in [draft, pending] - the published fix over-restricts a contributor trashing their own draft)
id supplied as a Relay global id or as a raw database id (both normalised by Utils::get_database_id_from_id at PostObjectUpdate.php:85)
update of a post authored by another user with/without authorId (authorId is re-derived before the edit_others_posts check at PostObjectUpdate.php:123-137)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: updateMediaItem -> MediaItemMutation::prepare_media_item() -> wp_update_post(): same post table sink, but the handler only checks the primitive cap->edit_posts plus an author comparison; it never calls current_user_can( $post_type_object->cap->edit_post, $media_item_id ), unlike PostObjectDelete.php:119 and MediaItemCreate.php:356 which do use object-level caps.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Attachments are a separate post type with their own mutation class and a status enum (inherit/private/trash/auto-draft, MediaItemStatusEnum.php:17-30) that has no publish state, so the advisory's publish/edit-published rules are argued not to cover media.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same directory, one file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Object-level edit_post gate for the media item, mirroring the new guard in PostObjectUpdate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The plugin's own convention already uses object-level caps in the two neighbouring media/post mutations (MediaItemCreate.php:356 checks cap->edit_post on the parent, PostObjectDelete.php:119 checks cap->delete_post), and MediaItemUpdate is a near-copy of PostObjectUpdate with that one line dropped.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An explicit publish rejection (UserError, mirroring rest_cannot_publish) for createPost instead of the silent pending downgrade
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer tightening the same capability family would naturally make create and update behave the same, and the REST parity comment in the published fix invites it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared prepare_post_object() that owns the status/capability decision for both create and update
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the single shared arg builder both mutations call; centralising the capability logic there is the obvious refactor and is exactly the over-broad fix that breaks createPost's downgrade contract.
